Obama often criticized Fox News. He also did fewer interviews with Fox News and took fewer questions from its correspondents compared to other news networks. His administration also said it was willing to exclude Fox News from interviews. Some accused his administration of blocking the network's access in one instance, but a spokesperson claimed it was a communication error and the administration backtracked.
However, the Obama administration never outright blocked, banned or ejected Fox News reporters from press briefings.
In September 2026, U.S. President Donald Trump banned three major news outlets — CNN, MSNOW and Politico — from the White House. The outlets subsequently filed a lawsuit accusing the administration of violating the First Amendment.
Soon after, former President Barack Obama condemned Trump's ban and speculated about the consequences if he had banned Fox News during his administration. In response, some people online claimed Obama had retaliated against Fox News (archived) in a similar way during his first term. For example, television personality Piers Morgan wrote on X (archived), "Obama did ban Fox, and waged almost constant war against press freedom."
(X user @PiersMorgan)
As Snopes previously reported in 2018, while Obama criticized Fox News and snubbed the network's requests for interviews, he never banned the network outright from the White House. As such, we rate this claim as mostly false.
In October 2009, a New York Times report (archived) stated Obama's Treasury Department attempted to exclude Fox News from a roundtable interview with the executive-pay czar Kenneth R. Feinberg. Major news networks were sharing a "pool" camera crew for these interviews. According to the report, other networks protested Fox's exclusion.
However, a 2009 Talking Points Memo report referred to the situation as a "miscommunication." The report said:
TPMDC dug into it, and here's what happened. Feinberg did a pen and pad with reporters to brief them on cutting executive compensation. TV correspondents, as they do with everything, asked to get the comments on camera. Treasury officials agreed and made a list of the networks who asked (Fox was not among them).
But logistically, all of the cameras could not get set up in time or with ease for the Feinberg interview, so they opted for a round robin where the networks use one pool camera. Treasury called the White House pool crew and gave them the list of the networks who'd asked for the interview.
The network pool crew noticed Fox wasn't on the list, was told that they hadn't asked and the crew said they needed to be included. Treasury called the White House and asked top Obama adviser Anita Dunn. Dunn said yes and Fox's Major Garrett was among the correspondents to interview Feinberg last night.
A Treasury spokesperson told Talking Points Memo, "There was no plot to exclude Fox News, and they had the same interview that their competitors did. Much ado about absolutely nothing." Fox News did conduct the interview with Feinberg.
The Obama administration didn't hold back in its criticism of Fox News in the aftermath of the controversy. When questioned by NBC News about the administration's tone regarding Fox News, Obama said:
We're going to take the media as it comes. And if media is operating basically as a talk radio format, then that's one thing, and if it's operating as a news outlet, then that's another. But it's not something I'm losing a lot of sleep over.
Obama spokesperson Josh Earnest reportedly admitted that the White House had demonstrated its "willingness to exclude Fox News" from interviews, but that it had not done so, according to Talking Points Memo. Earnest added, "The president and other high ranking officials and people like Ken Feinberg have done interviews with Fox in the past and will do them in the future."
In a 2010 interview with Rolling Stone, Obama accused Fox News of focusing more on its point of view than objectivity. "It's a point of view," Obama said, "that I think is ultimately destructive for the long-term growth of a country that has a vibrant middle class and is competitive in the world."
As Snopes previously reported, former Fox News White House correspondent Major Garrett asserted that though there was "never an effort to shut me out of the briefing room," ongoing tensions between the Obama administration and Fox News hindered his ability to do his job. In a November 2018 interview with The Hill, he said:
The White House would always pull me aside and say "well, really, Major, we're not at war with you," and I said "stop talking to me like that because when you're at war with my network you by definition are questioning and assailing my journalistic credibility and the work I do here every day," he said. "So don't tell me it's not about me, it is about me."
"Now, they never tried to pull my pass, but they had this sort of arms-length relationship to Fox and tried to demonize it on a daily basis. So that's another part of American history and journalism in the White House press corps I think at least should be noted at this moment," he said.
As we previously reported, Fox News' White House correspondents were called on less during press briefings compared to other major television networks. In September 2009, when Obama made the talk show rounds to talk about healthcare reform, he snubbed "Fox News Sunday" and did not appear on the show until his last year in office in 2016.
In 2013, The Washington Post reported that Obama's Department of Justice surveilled a Fox News reporter and obtained a search warrant for his emails while conducting an investigation into national security leaks in 2009. The investigation also looked into other reporters but appeared to specifically target Fox News.
The Obama administration never banned Fox News outright, but no love was lost between the two groups. While Fox News accused the administration of cutting it out of one interview, the administration blamed it on miscommunication and gave the network access while not hiding its disdain for the network.
For further reading, Snopes previously covered the misrepresented claim that former U.S. President Joe Biden cut reporters from the press pool.
Snopes' archives contributed to this report.

You can get Microsoft 365 for free through an eligible Education plan, free web and mobile versions of Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and other apps, or a 30-day Microsoft 365 trial with full desktop apps and 1 TB of OneDrive storage.
Microsoft 365 (formerly Office 365) is a subscription service that gives you access to various Microsoft products. This includes productivity apps like Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook, and OneNote; 1 TB of OneDrive cloud storage; and tools like Teams, Forms, and Loop.
As of writing, a paid subscription starts at $1.99 a month or $19.99 a year for Microsoft 365 Basic and goes up to $19.99 a month or $199.99 a year for Microsoft 365 Premium. Whether getting a subscription is justified depends on which of the included apps and services you use and how much.
If you’re not too sure about that and don’t want to buy a subscription right away, you can get Microsoft 365 for free using the following methods. Which method to pick depends on whether you’re a student/educator and your requirements.
Get the Microsoft 365 Education Plan
Microsoft 365 Education is a special plan for students and educators that provides free access to Microsoft 365 apps and services. You need a valid school, college, or university email address to be eligible. You’d have one if you’re a student or educator at an accredited institution with a Microsoft Education license.
To check if you qualify, visit the Microsoft 365 Education portal, type your institution-issued email address, and hit Next. If you’re eligible, you’ll be prompted to log in with the same email address. Or you may receive a verification link in your inbox. Subsequently, you’ll be able to use the Microsoft 365 apps within the browser or download them to your devices, based on the plan your institute offers.
Microsoft 365 Education is currently available in three plans: A1, A3, and A5. Your institute will most likely offer an A1 plan since it’s free, though some may offer an A3. The major difference between them is that A1 is web-only, whereas A3 supports downloads, so you can use the apps even when you’re offline.
If you don’t have an institute-provided email address or it isn’t eligible for the Education plan, you can get Microsoft 365 for free using the next method.

Use Microsoft 365 for the Web or Native Mobile Apps
Unless you have advanced needs — creating and running macros (VBA) in Excel, multi-device installation rights, or fully offline mode — you don’t really need a Microsoft 365 subscription. The online version of Microsoft 365, which offers access to basic versions of its apps, along with 5GB of free cloud storage, should serve your needs just as well.
All you need for this method is a Microsoft account and a web browser. In your preferred browser, visit the Microsoft 365 online portal and sign in with your Microsoft account. Create a new Microsoft account if you don’t have one.
Next, click the app launcher icon in your dashboard and select the app you want to use. This will open the app in a new browser tab, where you can create a new document or work on an existing one in your OneDrive storage. Any changes you make to the document are automatically saved to the cloud. Keep in mind, though, that the app’s functionality halts completely when you lose the internet connection.
Just like Microsoft 365 for the web, Microsoft also offers mobile apps for many of its productivity apps. So, if you just want to work on a Word, Excel, or PowerPoint document, you can download their mobile apps on your phone or tablet and use them. Just note that these apps offer limited functionality, similar to the web version. However, unlike their web versions, mobile apps support some offline functionality, allowing you to view a cached version of the document or edit local documents, even without an active internet connection.
Get the Microsoft 365 Free Trial
Microsoft offers a 30-day free trial to Microsoft 365. This trial gives you full, unrestricted access to the service, including complete offline capabilities and the ability to download desktop apps to your PC or Mac. You also get 1 TB of OneDrive cloud storage.
A free trial is great for someone who wants full-blown access to Microsoft’s productivity suite for a brief period. It also makes sense for those who want the Microsoft 365 service without committing to an upfront payment.
To subscribe to a 30-day Microsoft 365 free trial, you need a Microsoft account and a valid payment method. Open a browser and go to the official Microsoft 365 free trial page. Click the Start Free Trial button, and log in with your Microsoft account when prompted. If you haven’t taken a free trial with this account previously, you’ll be asked to add a valid payment method. Complete the checkout process. You now have complete access to Microsoft 365.
Set a reminder to cancel the subscription before the 30 days are up. If you forget, Microsoft will convert the trial to a monthly or annual subscription and charge you for the same on your added payment method.
Identify Your Use Case to Find the Right Method
You can use any of the above methods to get Microsoft 365 for free. However, not all of them offer the same level of access. As such, it’s important to identify your use case before choosing a method.
For example, if you want a full-blown Excel experience for a few weeks, the free 30-day trial makes more sense. Meanwhile, you might want to subscribe to the Microsoft 365 Education plan if you’re a student or educator and want desktop access to productivity apps for a longer period. Or use their mobile apps on your phone or tablet if you only need to view or maintain a few Excel sheets.

RFK Jr.'s ethics filing reveals book deals worth millions of dollars
RFK Jr.'s ethics disclosure reveals free travel and hefty book advances.
For stories on the science of healthy living, subscribe to NPR's Health newsletter.
In the minutes before Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. took the stage last Thursday at an anti-vaccine conference in Washington, D.C., MAHA Institute President Mark Gorton was calling vaccines "a public health disaster."
The conference was for Children's Health Defense, an anti-vaccine group that has filed dozens of lawsuits against federal agencies, state governments and companies over vaccine requirements and other policies it disagrees with.
Kennedy co-founded the group, and it paid him $326,056 in salary and bonuses in the year before he left his role as chairman of the board and chief legal counsel to lead the Department of Health and Human Services, according to a federal ethics filing.
"Let me be clear. You have a strong and steadfast friend at the White House," Kennedy told the crowd. "We've accomplished in 19 months … things that would have seemed unthinkable two years ago."
Talking to the anti-vaccine group he led so recently is just one of the ways Kennedy is pushing norms. He has also taken cash for book advances, defied his ethics agreement by promoting one of his books on social media and accepted expensive gifts.
"Having a secretary of health and human services not only give a keynote address at an anti-vaccine group that he helped found and continue to promote his anti-vaccine agenda is endangering the health, safety and lives of American citizens and the world at large," says Dr. Jason Goldman, the immediate past president of the American College of Physicians. "Nothing that I have seen with the current secretary of health and human services and his handling of public health and vaccines is, in my opinion, the norm."
The Department of Health and Human Services did not answer a detailed list of questions from NPR. Instead, the department emailed a statement that said, "Secretary Kennedy complies with all applicable federal ethics laws, regulations, and financial disclosure requirements. The Secretary works with HHS career ethics officials to ensure that his financial interests, gifts, outside activities, and other reportable matters are appropriately disclosed and handled consistent with those requirements."
Hefty advances for two books and pricey gifts
Kennedy reported in his latest financial disclosure, signed by an HHS ethics official on Sept. 17 and obtained by NPR afterward, that he received pricey flights from a friend to Fiji and Greece as well as lucrative book advances.
The two book advances were for $2 million apiece from Skyhorse Publishing, which has also published other books Kennedy wrote and also paid him $451,000 in consulting fees the year before he became HHS secretary.
One of the books in the works will be called Unsettled Science. The title is a twist on the term "settled science," often used to describe the evidence for vaccine safety.
Kennedy also received free flights to and from Fiji and Greece and the use of a vacation home in Washington, D.C. Their value totaled more than a quarter of a million dollars, according to the financial disclosure.
Those gifts were from Gavin de Becker, a celebrity security adviser who also wrote a book published by Skyhorse Publishing called Forbidden Facts. It alleges government suppression of information about brain damage from childhood vaccines.
The Kennedy disclosures are unusual, says Virginia Canter at Democracy Defenders Fund, a nonprofit that is focused on fighting corruption and protecting elections. "Those are large amounts of money for a government's public servant to receive while he is in office," she says.
In fact, the gifts and book advances are so large, that she had questions about whether they represent a "supplementation of salary" — something that's prohibited.
She says she would have expected to see the advances when Kennedy filed his initial report during the nomination and confirmation process in 2025. She says it was unusual to see them paid out during Kennedy's time as HHS secretary. "There are strict prohibitions on government officials, particularly those who serve as presidential appointees confirmed by the Senate, [and] the acceptance of what we call 'outside earned income.'"
As for the gifts from de Becker, Canter says, "I would really want to know more about the nature of their friendship. In other words, if it's a gift … based on a personal relationship, is he giving these gifts to all of his friends or is it just Mr. Kennedy?"
For his part, de Becker says the gifts are part of an ongoing friendship between the two men and their families.
"Bobby is my closest friend in the world for many years, and I'm grateful to be able to host him anytime," de Becker told NPR in an email. "He has hosted my family at his homes, he's stayed at mine, we take family vacations together every year, etc. I'm glad to be able to host him anytime, and I love the times our families spend traveling together. My gifts and our family vacations began years before he was at HHS — and I have nothing whatsoever to do with HHS in any regard."
Canter says Kennedy may have wealthy friends who can afford to treat him, but what's OK when you're in the private sector is different when you become a public servant.
The timing of the book advances is particularly noteworthy, she says, considering rules against outside income. If you're a public servant of Kennedy's rank, you aren't allowed to do any book writing — including taking notes — and get paid for it during your time in office.
Kathleen Clark, a law professor at Washington University in St. Louis who specializes in government ethics, agreed. "It seems very weird that RFK Jr. has accepted $4 million in book advances for two books that he has promised not to write or edit during the time that he's HHS Secretary," she says, referring to Kennedy's ethics agreement.
Kennedy also isn't supposed to promote his previous Skyhorse Publishing work, Clark says, citing his ethics agreement..
But in July, he posted from his personal social media account on X about a 2021 book he wrote criticizing Dr. Anthony Fauci, the director of the National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases from 1984 until 2022.
Kennedy's book, The Real Anthony Fauci, was published by Skyhorse Publishing, and according to Kennedy's ethics agreement, he declared, "During my appointment, I will not engage in any writing, editing, or promotional activities associated with these books and will not provide any other services under the publishing agreement."
Kennedy's latest financial disclosure itself was filed very late. It was due May 15, and they're usually posted publicly within 30 days. Kennedy's was filed Aug. 13, or 90 days late, after receiving an extension. It was then revised four times in September before ethics officials provided it to NPR.
The document has been approved by ethics officials at HHS, but the separate Office of Government Ethics had not yet signed off.
The Gardasil lawsuit
The filing did not fully settle an ongoing question about whether Kennedy or his family made money from his involvement in a legal case against a vaccine company he now regulates.
Kennedy reported in his annual filing that he received a nearly $7,000 payment from Wisner Baum, a law firm that was suing the drug company Merck over claims that it failed to properly warn consumers about risks from its HPV vaccine, Gardasil.
Kennedy's disclosure listed the Wisner Baum payment as "final payment at termination of agreement of Referral Fees On Contingency Fee Case."
But the law firm told NPR it wasn't related to the Gardasil case.
For context, Kennedy's original financial disclosure and ethics agreement from 2025, he planned to collect 10% through contingency fees in the Gardasil case and had received $856,559 in contingency fees from Wisner Baum from other cases in the year prior.
That worried members of congress, like Sen. Elizabeth Warren, a Massachusetts Democrat, during the confirmation process.
"You go online, you do commercials to encourage people to sign up with Wisner Baum to join lawsuits against vaccine makers," Warren said during the Jan. 29, 2025 hearing. "And for everyone who signs up, you personally get paid, and if they win their case, you get 10% of what they win. So, if you bring in someone who gets $10 million, you walk away with a million dollars."
Afterward, Kennedy amended his ethics agreement, stating that he would "irrevocably assign my right to receive payment in all outstanding contingency fee cases … to a non-dependent, adult family member."
In early June, Merck agreed to settle the lawsuit.
Merck issued the following statement: "After a thorough review of the body of evidence that supports the safety and efficacy profile of our HPV vaccines, both parties in the litigation concluded that it was appropriate to end the litigation in its entirety, resolving all but one case in an amount that is considerably less than Merck's anticipated costs of defense in the litigation and that is not material to Merck."
Neither Merck nor Wisner Baum would comment on the size of the settlement. According to other reports, it was $50 million.
A group of lawmakers in July questioned whether a Kennedy family member was profiting from the settlement, to which Kennedy responded on social media that the fees went "back to the Wisner Baum law firm," something that isn't in his records filed with the Office of Government Ethics.
Kennedy's son Conor is a lawyer at Wisner Baum. He's listed on its website as an associate attorney, but the Gardasil case is not included in his firm profile.
Wisner Baum says, "Secretary Kennedy has not received any fees recovered from the Gardasil cases, nor has anyone in his family."

During a tense vote on a data center being built in her drought-stricken Arizona district last summer, Tucson City Councilmember Nikki Lee made an unlikely pitch: “We’re going to get a little out-of-this-world for a second, so just bear with me.”
Google is sending a data center into space
What Big Tech’s sci-fi dream reveals about the infrastructure America actually needs.
Like many of her constituents, Lee did not want Project Blue, a sprawling 290-acre data center, gobbling up an ounce of her local drinking water. “We need to put data centers where they belong,” she said, and “we don’t think data centers belong in the desert.”
President Donald Trump’s recent bluster aside, it’s possible that the only thing as bipartisan as loving Dolly Parton is hating data centers, whose construction has become so controversial, so costly, and so backlogged here on Earth that companies like Google, Meta, and of course, SpaceX, are actively flirting with the idea of flinging them into orbit instead. Soon after the Tucson City Council rejected Project Blue’s attempt to connect to city utilities, Amazon Web Services, the secretive intended beneficiary, pulled out of the project, and another Jeff Bezos company, Blue Origin, filed a plan with regulators for tens of thousands of possible new data centers, this time, destined for orbit.
Sure, launching a hyperscale AI data center into space is still unprecedented engineering-wise, carries an unfathomably large price tag, could engender its own severe environmental risks, and may or may not draw unwelcome attention from the hunters among the stars. But for AI companies, such trade-offs might still be preferable to the terrestrial roadblocks, among them an explosive populist backlash and a 12-year wait to connect to the power grid.
Next Thursday, Google plans to launch a pilot satellite capable of processing basic AI queries into orbit, the most significant test yet in what’s become a burgeoning race to power AI from space. For now, the satellite won’t approach the levels of computing power at a hulking terrestrial data center like Project Blue. But it is a major step toward a future in which many or even most of our AI queries will be powered not from the outskirts of a city like Tucson, but from a blinking data center circling the skies.
SpaceX’s gargantuan initial public offering earlier this summer was predicated on the idea that it would launch a thus-far-unrealized fleet of orbital data centers to fuel much of the AI economy. The company — whose rockets Google will use to launch its pilot — claims that by the end of this decade, possibly as early as 2028, it will have successfully assembled an AI data center in orbit, with plans to eventually harvest a staggering 100 gigawatts of new solar energy for AI annually, equivalent to one-fifth of all US electricity consumption last year. (As always, that’s a very iffy promise.)
Still, as Google’s overtures clearly demonstrate, it’s no longer a question of if large-scale space-based data centers could be technically feasible, but rather when they’ll be ready to launch, and perhaps more importantly, whether the math of using them to power something like AI will make much financial sense anytime soon. As of now, building a one-gigawatt data center in space would cost about $51.5 billion, according to an analysis by aerospace engineer Andrew McCalip, compared with $16 billion for one on land.
“They’re not breaking any rules of physics. Yes, there are going to be engineering challenges, but they are all solvable with enough time and money,” said Jason Aspiotis, a leading space systems engineer who now leads an orbital data center startup. “The gray area is, well, what about the economics?”
But even if this astronomically kooky plan does take off, it may not change much for those of us left on terra firma: Our energy bills will remain high, even if data centers aren’t there to drive them up. Our earthly infrastructure — affordable housing, public transit, and more — may be just as hard to build as ever. Harder even, maybe, given that crucial resources and untapped tax revenue will be literally rocketing up out of our reach.
No, if these tech giants succeed, it will not fix what’s wrong here on Earth, but merely prove once again their exemption to the gravitational forces holding the rest of us down.
Space-based data centers, explained
My father spent most of his career working in the satellite industry, and would sometimes let me waltz inside the quaint little data center housed in his office, a room I remember as roughly the size of my school’s computer lab, hosting rows upon rows of servers that I couldn’t touch, churning with a cool, mechanical hum as they crunched zeroes and ones.
AI data centers work similarly to that server room but on an exponentially larger scale, requiring far more land and energy to run, and much more extravagant cooling systems. Sending his office’s data center into orbit would have been extraordinarily difficult, and getting one of the facilities that powers modern LLMs aloft would be an even larger, more ambitious undertaking. But the benefits — namely, “cheap space (no pun intended) and power,” as my dad put it to me recently — are even more enticing.
An orbital data center need not negotiate with an elected official like Lee over precious water rights to the Colorado River, though it would need to install bigger-than-football-field-sized heat radiators to keep itself cool. You can’t simply launch something that big into orbit, meaning a space-based hyperscale data center — the size of which would likely rival that of the International Space Station — would need to be assembled piece by piece, probably by robots. And while the sun would provide an endless supply of solar power to process your ChatGPT queries, it would also inflict incessant radiation on delicate circuitry. If something breaks, you can’t send a technician up to fix it. Many experts are also concerned that if an excess of space junk, which extraterrestrial data centers would inevitably produce, begins colliding like bumper cars in Earth’s low orbit, it could knock out the orbital infrastructure we already rely on, like GPS navigation and weather satellites.
Even plastic decays in space, said Sven Bilén, a professor of aerospace engineering at Penn State, who, like Aspiotis, believes that early orbital data centers will probably be “processing data from space, like spatial imaging satellites or weather satellites, as opposed to, you know, cat videos” or AI-generated reality TV slop.
But even if AI is not the lowest-hanging fruit for deploying compute into space, it is certainly the deepest-pocketed, meaning that many investors and companies like SpaceX and Google seem quite willing to shoulder the start-up costs anyway. And considering how difficult it’s gotten to build data centers on Earth, or at least in the United States, it’s indeed possible that space could become the cheaper, or at least most convenient option, more quickly than one might think.
“In some form or another, in five years, we are going to have some orbital data centers in space for sure,” Krishna Muralidharan, who leads the Center for Semiconductor Manufacturing at the University of Arizona, told me, but it’s hard to say right now whether those consist of just a few expensive prototypes, or the beginning of a much bigger swing toward orbital compute. “Only time will tell whether you’re going to have a business case for it.”
Can we send our data center problem into space?
So, is it better to have a data center in space or in your backyard?
David Reid, a member of Virginia’s House of Delegates representing Loudoun County, home to more data centers than anywhere else on Earth, says the question has repeatedly come up at his town hall meetings. Reid is the rare politician — apart from the president, anyway — willing to defend terrestrial data centers, calling them a “money-printing machine” for local schools and infrastructure. Having spent decades working in the defense and technology sectors, he is doubtful that the math on orbital data centers will ever make sense.
“I believe this is, for lack of a better term, fictional nonsense,” he said, and is “creating a distraction from the fact that local officials here on Earth still need to make better zoning decisions.”
If most of the AI industry can eventually be powered by space, as SpaceX claims, it will require millions of sprawling new satellites, in an orbit currently dotted by fewer than 20,000 of them. Though “space is really big,” as Elon Musk has put it, one million satellites would still profoundly and, likely irrevocably, transform our night sky into one in which data centers outnumber visible stars.
“Will humanity notice if there are fewer stars in the sky? Well, not so much right now,” given light pollution in many cities, said John Barentine, an astronomer and environmental advocate for the night sky. “But what if they’re replaced by these artificial stars in the night sky? Is that the point at which people will say, ‘Wait a minute, we don’t want this. We want the benefits, but we don’t want this as a consequence.’”
This is, of course, the tension also at the heart of building data centers here on Earth. To some extent, they’re the most tangible representations of how little power we have to shape the course of a transformative new technology that few trust, and even fewer asked for. It’s one thing to object to a hulking data center, but it might be another altogether to see the sigils of our digital overlords illuminating the firmament. Would a place like Tucson, one of the most beautiful places to stargaze in the world, prefer a Project Blue to a starscape marred by blinking servers in the sky?

A Westbury High School student was shot dead near the Houston ISD campus on Friday morning, reported the Houston Police Department. "Someone came out of a wooded area nearby at a nearby [apartment] complex and from that we believe some words were exchanged and someone produced a handgun and unfortunately someone lost their life as a result of what I call a cowardly act," Diaz stated in a press conference in the morning. Although an investigation has been launched. "We're working diligently to make sure we get someone in custody as soon as possible," said the officer, as per ABC News. Diaz said that the team probing the shooting “have an idea of who we're looking for.” "I'm saddened by the loss," Diaz said, adding that "it shouldn't have happened." "Keep this family in your prayers. These kinds of events shouldn't be happening in our community," Diaz further said. The victim’s family is “devastated,” police reportedly added. The family has not yet reacted to the incident publicly. “A grandmother shouldn’t be on the side of the street here, grieving for her child, for her grandchild. A statement from the Houston Independent School District's press office said that "Secure" mode operations took place at the high school during an HPD investigation after the shooting. Reportedly, classes continued at the high school. Students were able to attend their respective sessions. The world has known for decades that the RSA cryptosystem’s days are numbered. Once quantum computing becomes practical (estimates for that range from 3 to 20 or more years), the foundational security it provides will crumble. New research has revealed a novel method that uses classical computing to reduce the current RSA security level to an unacceptably low threshold.
The finding poses little to no practical threat in the immediate term, except possibly in a few edge cases. Even applying the attack against the deprecated use of 1024-bit keys, the method requires more computation than just about anybody—short of nation-states or companies with massive resources—can achieve. Widely used RSA implementations are also safe.
Nonetheless, the research has taken cryptographers by surprise because it introduces signature forgery, a new way to break RSA keys without factoring. Equally important, this novel method reduces the required computing resources by orders of magnitude.
Out of reach no more
“If this result holds up under peer review, it would indeed be a conceptual break-through,” Karsten Nohl, a cryptography expert and the head of innovation at Allurity, said in an interview. “RSA is as difficult to break as it is to factor large integers, at least so we thought. The researcher suggests that you can practically break RSA without cracking its key.”
Nadia Heninger, a University of California at San Diego professor and lead author, elaborated:
Cryptographers thought that the only way to compute valid RSA digital signatures was to first compute the private key by factoring, and then use the private key to compute the signatures. For 1024-bit RSA, this was thought to be very expensive, albeit probably doable if you have the computational resources of the large tech companies or the NSA—on the order of tens of millions of dollars of computation time for a single key. For 2048-bit RSA, it was thought to be totally out of reach.
The key forgery attack Heninger and the other researchers devised brings the breakage of 1024-bit RSA into the realm of possibility much sooner than previously estimated. Even for 2048- and 4096-bit keys, the method reduces the security of RSA to unacceptable levels. The National Security Agency, National Institute of Standards and Technology, and European Union Agency for Network and Information Security require that any cryptosystem should provide a level of no less than 128 or more bits, meaning the operations required must exceed 2128.

With cases of mumps being reported from various parts of Thrissur district in Keralam, the District Medical Officer (DMO) has urged the public to remain vigilant.
Mumps is a viral infection that spreads through air, particularly through droplets from coughing and sneezing, nasal secretions and close contact with infected persons. The disease is most contagious from about two days before the onset of swelling to four to six days after the swelling appears.
Children between five and 15 years are commonly affected, although adults can also contract the infection. The disease can be more severe in adults.
Symptoms
The most prominent symptom is swelling on the sides of the cheeks, below the ears. The swelling may affect one or both sides of the face. Mild fever and headache are among the early symptoms, followed by difficulty in opening the mouth, chewing and swallowing. Loss of appetite and fatigue may also occur.
The DMO has advised patients to seek treatment for fever and pain, drink plenty of fluids and take adequate rest. If proper precautions are not taken, the infection can, in some cases, affect the brain, testicles, ovaries, pancreas and prostate. Complications such as encephalitis may occur if the infection spreads to the brain. In adults, complications involving the reproductive organs can, in some cases, affect fertility.
Avoid contact
Teachers should immediately inform parents and health workers if children develop symptoms. Infected persons should remain at home until they have recovered. They should avoid close contact with others. Children with mumps should not be sent to school.
Disinfecting items used by infected persons, wearing masks, maintaining physical distance and washing hands with soap are among the measures recommended to prevent the spread of the infection. The illness usually subsides within one to two weeks.
MMR vaccine
The DMO has advised parents to ensure that children receive the MMR (measles, mumps and rubella) vaccine at 16-24 months of age, as it provides protection against the three infections.
Anyone developing symptoms has been advised to consult a doctor promptly and seek appropriate treatment.

A video circulating on social media claims to show massive flames and thick black smoke following an airstrike on an airport in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia (here, here, here). Even a few mainstream media outlets reported these visuals with the same claim (here, here). Let’s verify the claim made in the post.
Claim: Video shows an airstrike on Riyadh Airport in Saudi Arabia.
Fact: This video is not from Riyadh. It shows a fire caused by a drone strike at the Sadovod market in Moscow, Russia, in June 2026. While there were reports of a Houthi attack on Riyadh airport in September 2026, the viral video is unrelated to that incident. Hence, the claim made in the post is MISLEADING.
We conducted a reverse image search of the viral video and found the same visuals in multiple videos published on 18 June 2026 (here, here & here). These reports confirm that the footage is from Moscow, Russia, and shows a fire at the Sadovod market following a drone attack.
According to news reports (here & here), the Sadovod market in Moscow was engulfed in flames and smoke following a drone strike on 18 June 2026. We also checked the location using Google Street View, and the surroundings seen in the viral video match the Sadovod market in Moscow, confirming that the footage is from Moscow.
However, several international news outlets (here & here) reported that the Houthis claimed to have targeted “sensitive sites” in Riyadh on 19 September 2026. On the same day, a fire broke out at a fuel storage depot near King Khalid International Airport, with large flames and thick black smoke visible from the area.
To sum up, an old Russian video is being shared as visuals showing an airstrike on Riyadh Airport.

Rick Wakeman has played to all kinds of people around the globe, but he has now performed to an audience he had never encountered before – an enclosure of 150 bears.
The former Yes musician, who has gone on to have a prolific solo career, played the piano at a Vietnamese bear sanctuary.
“Before you ask, I won’t be playing the teddy bear’s picnic,” he joked ahead of the performance. Wakeman, who is a supporter of animal welfare causes and has rescue dogs and cats of his own, is conducting the concert to raise awareness of moon bears kept in cruel conditions for the extraction of their bile.
He said he was a bit worried about how hot it is going to be. “You know the heatwave we had in England? It’s double that,” he said. “They offered to rig up a fan for me, but I figured that will just blow more hot air around.”
His concert was performed live on a Yamaha grand piano positioned in Animals Asia’s bear sanctuary in the Tam Dao national park, and Wakeman had written some new compositions especially for rescued bears.
Asked whether the bears would enjoy the music, he said: “They’ve not got much choice, really. It’s a well-known fact that all animals react to music, especially gentle melodic music. So what I am going to do is piano music that is melodic, and I can only hope that they will come up to the perimeter of the sanctuary and have a listen.”
Wakeman has been sponsoring rescue bears since 2016 and recently adopted a new one: “He’s only 20 months old, a big fella, I went to see him today. He came out right to the edge and stood on his back legs and just stared at me, it was brilliant.”
Bile is extracted from bears for traditional Chinese medicine by putting a needle into their gall bladder and drawing it out. The bears are kept in poor conditions in countries including China and in Vietnam, where it has just been banned, but where some bears are still in captivity in cramped enclosures. It is the fourth-biggest market in the illegal wildlife trade in east Asia, resulting in a dramatic decline in the Asiatic black bear populations in Vietnam, with nearly a third of their numbers lost around the world in just 30 years.
Of the sanctuary, which he has been visiting this week, Wakeman said: “To see the bears be rehabilitated, having a life they never had before, some have never put their feet on grass before. They are so wonderful, that we can do such horrendous things to animals is beyond belief. Before this, they were chained in cages sometimes for 10 or 20 years in conditions where they couldn’t even turn around.”
He is playing to raise awareness for the bears still stuck in cages in Vietnam and to urge the government to get them released: “We have 150 bears at the sanctuary, but there are 125 bears left in cages in the old bear bile farms, and there are four dying a month. We have to get them out quick and into the sanctuary.”
He treats his rescue dogs and cats to music back at home in Suffolk. “I had one cat who used to jump on the grand piano, and if I stopped playing he would put his paw in the strings and rattle them until I played again. I know if my dogs don’t like it, they will get up and walk out, and my cats don’t like metal, grunge or rap. They want a melody.”
Wakeman spends hours watching the bears. “If you see these bears it is hard to put into words, they are almost human the way they look at you,” he said. “If you see them, you can’t help but be moved. They aren’t tame but they are very safe, very happy, they play, they romp. I witnessed two today jumping in a bubble bath and playing. They’ve got a life back.”
Dr Jill Robinson, the founder and CEO of Animals Asia, said: “We are beyond blessed to have Rick’s support for Animals Asia and the bears. His love for them is immeasurable and can be heard in the beautifully haunting music he has written for them. We’re all so excited to hear his performance in the open air at our sanctuary in the stunning setting of Tam Dao national park. I can’t wait to see how the bears respond.”
Wakeman added: “I hope they lay down and have a listen, that would make my day. I would have a big grin on my face.”

A month after Nepal floods, families await answers about missing Ukrainians
Olena Kalynychenko is among thousands missing after devastating floods hit the Nepal-China border
BANGKOK -- Olena Kalynychenko was looking forward to sharing the chrysanthemum tea she had bought in China with her partner.
“She said, ‘When I come back home, we will drink the tea made from Chinese flowers,’” said Oles Visich, Kalynychenko’s partner. He has now been waiting for news about her for a month, after she and thousands of others disappeared in catastrophic flooding along the Nepal-China border.
Her last known location was exiting China at a border post at 10:22 a.m. local time, 15 minutes before the flood.
Kalynychenko, 36, was part of a group of 56 people, mostly Ukrainians, who had traveled to Mount Kailash in Tibet for a spiritual retreat.
Their families' situation is a sign of how complex and time-consuming the process is of rescuing, recovering and identifying victims lost to the disaster. Given the number of missing, the process will likely take months.
They disappeared while heading from China to Nepal on their way home. Some relatives say they have received no information from authorities. The Chinese government has told at least two families that their relatives left Chinese territory before the flood struck, but they haven't been able to confirm whether they entered Nepal as Nepal's immigration complex and its records were destroyed in the floods.
The floods killed more than 1,400 people and left more than 6,000 missing, most of them on the Nepali side of the border. Nepal has said that 636 foreign nationals remain missing, including 54 Ukrainians. China has reported 261 foreign nationals among the missing on its side, including one Ukrainian.
Families in Ukraine say most of them have not received any answers since realizing their relatives were among the missing.
“We only have the statistics that are being posted online — how many people have been found, how many are alive, how many are dead, and how many are still missing,” said Stanislav Solohub, whose brother and sister-in-law went missing on Aug. 25.
Nepal says it has recovered 1,451 bodies, but only 112 have been handed over to families so far.
The government said it has collected DNA samples from 2,035 relatives so far, but it has not disclosed how many victims have been identified.
The group, led by Irina Blonskaya, a spiritual teacher who often organized retreats, was returning from its journey home in China when the flood struck Aug. 26. Their plan was to travel by bus from the Tibet region to Kathmandu, where its members would board flights to their respective countries. The group’s last message was sent at 8:27 a.m. Nepal time, about 10 minutes before the mountain slope collapsed.
Many had not checked in with their loved ones that morning, owing to the time difference.
Authorities have said the were triggered when a section of ice and rock broke away from a Himalayan mountain slope, creating a fast-moving torrent of water, ice, mud and debris. It destroyed communities and Gyirong Port, a border crossing used by some pilgrims traveling to or returning from Mount Kailash.
Vladsylava Horlova’s mother, Elena, was traveling in the group as well. She initially found her mother’s name of the list of the missing from the Nepali government, but hasn't received any further information from the Nepali side. Later, the Chinese embassy confirmed her mother had left the country, and was not counted in China's list of missing people.
Horlova, a college student who is a refugee in Norway, worries her mother wasn't in either country when the flood struck. There’s a stretch of road between the Nepali immigration building and the Chinese one along the border, videos from travelers show.
“You think about what if someone appeared to be in a no man’s land or that they left China, but not physically, who’s looking for them?” she asked.
Horlova has attempted to contact organizations ranging from the Ukrainian embassy in China, to Norwegian police, and even the Red Cross. She, like the others, have submitted their DNA samples to police to help the search.
On the other side of the border, China has said that when the remains of foreigners are identified, it will notify their respective embassies, but the authorities have not given any details about how many identities have been confirmed so far.
Though it has been a month since the original disaster, some families are still holding on to hope.
Just days before Kalynychenko left for her travels, she organized a retreat for women in Ukraine whose partners were fighting on the front lines of the war, some of whom had not heard from their partners for two years.
Visich, her partner, sees the irony of his situation, but like others in the group, has chosen to stay positive. Visich, also a psychologist, wrote a support guide for others like himself, offering tips on mental health.
“Because for my Olenka, for example, the most important thing in our connection, that each other … needs to be happy,” Visich said.

AP writer Binaj Gurubacharya in Kathmandu, Nepal and senior video producer Volodymr Yurchuk in Kyiv, Ukraine contributed to this report.

Current Bharat NCAP phase remains valid until Sept 30, 2027, with proposed introduction of Bharat NCAP 2.0 from Oct 2027
Bharat NCAP 2.0, planned for October 2027, will look beyond what happens when a car crashes. The proposed system will examine the entire safety chain: from how a vehicle helps avoid a collision to how well it protects occupants, pedestrians and other vulnerable road users, and what happens after an accident.Union road transport and highways minister Nitin Gadkari announced the proposed timeline at the SIAM Annual Convention in September 2026. The second phase is being planned as the first phase of Bharat New Car Assessment Programme, or Bharat NCAP, approaches the end of its current cycle.According to the ministry of road transport and highways’ draft AIS-197 Revision 1, the first phase of Bharat NCAP began on October 1, 2023 and is valid until September 30, 2027. The draft revision has been prepared as the framework for Bharat NCAP 2.0.The proposed changes could make the safety rating a much broader measure of a car’s performance, not just in a crash, but before, during and after one.
About Bharat NCAP
What is Bharat NCAP?
Bharat NCAP is India’s own vehicle crash-testing and safety-rating programme. It was formally launched by the ministry of road transport and highways in August 2023 and became operational from October 1, 2023.
The programme applies to type-approved passenger vehicles in the M1 category with a gross vehicle weight of less than 3.5 tonnes. It is voluntary, which means manufacturers can offer eligible vehicles for assessment.The programme is anchored by the Central Institute of Road Transport (CIRT), while testing is carried out through designated agencies with the required infrastructure.At its core, Bharat NCAP gives car buyers a common safety benchmark. A vehicle must already meet mandatory regulatory requirements to be sold in India. Bharat NCAP goes a step further by putting eligible vehicles through specified tests and awarding them a rating of between one and five stars.
India's own car safety assessment programme
The idea is fairly simple: instead of looking only at a car’s price, design or features, buyers get an additional reference point to understand how the vehicle performs in standardised safety tests.The government has also positioned the programme as a way to encourage manufacturers to improve vehicle safety and strengthen the safety standards of cars made in India.
How does the current Bharat NCAP system work?
The existing programme broadly assesses three areas:
Adult Occupant Protection (AOP)
Child Occupant Protection (COP)
Safety Assist Technologies (SAT)
Vehicles are subjected to prescribed crash tests and other assessments. Their performance across these parameters is then used to arrive at the overall star rating.The current framework includes a 64 kmph offset frontal impact test, a 50 kmph side movable deformable barrier test and a pole side impact test, among other checks prescribed under AIS-197.The assessment therefore goes beyond simply asking whether the passenger compartment remains intact.Adult Occupant Protection examines the risk of injury to adults in different crash conditions and seating positions. Child Occupant Protection looks at the protection offered to younger passengers, including the use and installation of child restraint systems.Safety Assist Technologies, meanwhile, covers technologies designed to help prevent crashes or reduce their severity.
Quote
Why are adult and child safety assessed separately?
A car may offer different levels of protection to adults and children, so Bharat NCAP evaluates the two separately.The adult assessment focuses on occupant protection during prescribed crash scenarios, while the child assessment considers how effectively younger occupants are protected and how child restraint systems work within the vehicle.This also means that a car’s overall star rating is not simply a score from one crash test. It reflects performance across several safety parameters.For consumers, the individual scores can therefore provide more information than looking at the star rating alone.
Who tests the cars?
Bharat NCAP is anchored by CIRT, with testing carried out through designated testing agencies that have the required facilities.The wider automotive testing ecosystem includes agencies such as the Automotive Research Association of India (ARAI) and the International Centre for Automotive Technology (ICAT).Manufacturers submit eligible vehicles for assessment under the programme. The existing framework specifies procedures around the variant selected for testing, including provisions concerning the base variant of a model.That distinction matters when reading a Bharat NCAP result. A rating should not automatically be assumed to apply to every variant of a model unless the official assessment covers those variants.
Four assessments of NCAP
Bharat NCAP ratings
Bharat NCAP ratings range from one to five stars. A higher rating indicates stronger performance under the programme’s prescribed assessment criteria.But a five-star rating is not a guarantee that occupants will escape injury in every real-world crash. NCAP testing is conducted under standardised conditions and is intended to provide a basis for comparing vehicle safety performance.It is also important to distinguish Bharat NCAP from the mandatory certification requirements for selling a vehicle in India.Bharat NCAP is voluntary and is designed to provide consumers with additional information beyond the mandatory regulatory framework. A vehicle being tested or rated under Bharat NCAP should therefore not be confused with regulatory approval.Since its launch, Bharat NCAP has increasingly become part of the safety conversation around new car launches. The ratings have also become a factor in how manufacturers present their vehicles to consumers, particularly as safety becomes a more visible consideration in the passenger-vehicle market.
What do the stars represent?
So, what changes with Bharat NCAP 2.0?
This is where the proposed second phase takes a much wider approach.The draft AIS-197 Revision 1 divides Bharat NCAP 2.0 into five safety verticals:
Safe driving
Crash avoidance
Crash protection
Vulnerable road user protection
Post-crash safety
The change is significant because the current system focuses mainly on occupant protection and safety-assist technologies, while the proposed framework looks at the complete safety chain.The draft framework uses a 100-point assessment structure, with Crash Protection accounting for 55% of the assessment. The remaining weightage covers the other safety areas.In other words, the crash itself will still be a major part of the rating, but it will no longer be the only part of the safety story.
Five crash tests in the proposed new framework
Bharat NCAP 2.0 proposes expanding the Crash Protection assessment to five mandatory crash tests:
64 kmph offset frontal impact against a deformable barrier
50 kmph frontal impact against a full-width rigid barrier
50 kmph lateral impact against a mobile deformable barrier
32 kmph oblique side impact against a rigid pole
50 kmph rear impact against a mobile rigid barrier
Adult and child occupant protection will continue to be assessed separately.The addition of full-width frontal and rear-impact tests means the proposed system will examine crash scenarios beyond the core tests in the existing framework.That gives the second phase a wider testing footprint and allows different types of impacts to form part of the overall safety assessment.
Not just about surviving crash
One of the biggest differences in Bharat NCAP 2.0 is that the programme is designed to look at what happens before a crash as well.Crash Avoidance is one of the five proposed verticals. It focuses on technologies and vehicle characteristics that can help prevent a collision or reduce its severity.
Your guide to safer cars
Safe Driving is another proposed category, widening the assessment beyond the vehicle’s passive protection features.Together, these categories shift the focus from simply asking, “How well does this car perform when it crashes?” to a broader question: “How does this vehicle contribute to safety across different stages of a road incident?”Bharat NCAP 2.0 also proposes a separate Vulnerable Road User Protection category. This brings pedestrians and other vulnerable road users more directly into the safety assessment.The proposed framework also asks a different question: what happens once the collision has taken place?Post-Crash Safety is one of the five proposed assessment areas. Minister Gadkari described Bharat NCAP 2.0 as covering the entire safety chain, including post-crash evacuation and care. “We are going to evaluate the entire crash chain,” Gadkari said, adding that new technologies developed globally as well as by startups would be considered under the programme.This means the assessment is intended to extend beyond the instant of impact and examine safety considerations in the period immediately after a crash.It adds another layer to the programme’s approach: avoiding the crash where possible, protecting people during the impact, and addressing safety after the collision.
What does Bharat NCAP mean for car buyers?
For buyers, Bharat NCAP offers an additional way to compare cars beyond mandatory safety requirements.A consumer can look at a vehicle’s overall rating as well as its adult and child protection performance and the safety technologies considered in the assessment.The rating is not meant to replace other factors involved in buying a car. Price, size, fuel efficiency, features, driving requirements and other considerations remain relevant, but the proposed 2.0 framework would expand that information further.Buyers could eventually have a broader picture of how a car performs across crash protection, crash avoidance, safe driving, vulnerable-road-user protection and post-crash safety.Bharat NCAP is one part of a much larger road-safety challenge, focusing on the structure of vehicles. Vehicle design and safety technology can influence the outcome of a crash, but they cannot address every reason why accidents happen.The ministry has identified several factors associated with road crashes, including speeding, mobile-phone use, drunken driving, wrong-side driving, lane indiscipline, jumping red lights and failure to use helmets and seat belts. Vehicle condition, road conditions and weather can also play a role.
Several countries have their own NCAPS
Government data recorded 1,68,491 road accident fatalities in 2022.Bharat NCAP therefore addresses one part of this wider equation: the safety performance of vehicles. Its proposed second phase would broaden that role by looking at what a vehicle can do to help avoid crashes, how it protects people when a crash occurs, how it protects vulnerable road users and what happens afterwards.
The bottom line
The current Bharat NCAP phase remains valid until September 30, 2027. The government has proposed introducing Bharat NCAP 2.0 from October 2027, with the draft AIS-197 Revision 1 serving as the framework for the next phase.The proposed transition would take India’s vehicle safety-rating system from a relatively focused crash and occupant-protection programme to a broader safety assessment.
The familiar one-to-five-star rating would remain the consumer-facing language of vehicle safety, but the assessment behind it is set to become much more comprehensive.The bigger shift is in the question Bharat NCAP is trying to answer. Instead of looking only at how a car performs when it is involved in a crash, the proposed system would examine the vehicle’s safety journey from avoiding a collision to protecting occupants and vulnerable road users, and supporting safety after the crash.That could give Indian car buyers a wider set of safety information to consider when choosing their next vehicle.

NEW DELHI: Unease within the ruling National Democratic Alliance (NDA) over a media report concerning Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar surfaced on Friday, with three BJP allies urging the Election Commission of India (ECI) to issue a clearer response.Union minister and Lok Janshakti Party (LJP) president Chirag Paswan was the first NDA ally to urge the ECI to dispel “misgivings in the minds of the people.”“Let me make it clear that, as part of the government, I do not intend to defend what is a constitutional body. I am also not much worried about the allegations made by the opposition, which will always take a stand that suits it politically,” Paswan told reporters in Patna.“However, if people start losing trust in the electoral system, that will not augur well for democracy. Therefore, I think the Election Commission must come out with its clarification more forcefully. It need not respond to what Rahul Gandhi and his associates are saying, but it must dispel misgivings in the minds of the people,” the Hajipur MP added.Rashtriya Lok Morcha (RLM) chief and Rajya Sabha MP Upendra Kushwaha also called for a clarification, saying the controversy had created “confusion” among the public.
"The controversy regarding the SIR has created a situation of significant confusion among the public. The matter needs to be addressed. The Election Commission should immediately issue a clarification regarding the actual situation to clear up this confusion," Kushwaha posted on X.The Telugu Desam Party (TDP) described the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise in Andhra Pradesh as a “success,” while noting that a clarification from the ECI would be “beneficial”.“The exercise has been a success. Even the opposition has not been able to substantiate its concerns regarding the process in Andhra Pradesh. At the same time, the Election Commission of India is a constitutional institution entrusted with a crucial responsibility in our democracy. Therefore, whenever questions are raised by anyone, providing appropriate clarification and maintaining transparency will only help strengthen public confidence in the institution,” TDP MP Lavu Srikrishna Devarayalu said.
What is the controversy
The allies’ remarks came after a report in The Indian Express said Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had, on at least 14 occasions over the past 10 months, recorded objections to decisions and orders apparently issued without their knowledge or recommendation.The objections reportedly related to changes to the statutory voter registration Form 6, the process for adding and deleting names from electoral rolls, and the centralised control of the electoral roll database.The report prompted opposition parties to demand the CEC’s removal and call for the SIR exercise to be halted.The ECI, however, asserted that differences of opinion among its members were a “normal part of deliberation” and maintained that its final decisions, including those concerning the SIR, had been “unanimous”.According to the Commission, all its official orders and directions had legal sanction, while describing the suggestions made by the two Election Commissioners as efforts to improve electoral processes. Neither Sandhu nor Joshi has publicly commented on the objections attributed to them.The BJP, meanwhile, has played down the reported differences within the Commission, saying that the exchange of views during official deliberations reflected “pure democracy." The saffron party's West Bengal unit chief, Samik Bhattacharya, for instance,
suggested that Gyanesh Kumar be awarded the Padma Bhushan, the country's third-highest civilan honour."The fact is, even the Congress party itself doesn't heed Rahul Gandhi's words; they don't take him seriously... Gyanesh Kumar deserves, at the very least, the Padma Bhushan... In a border state like this (West Bengal), Gyanesh Kumar took the initiative to remove the names of Bangladeshi infiltrators from the voter list," Bhattacharya said.Kumar, who became an Election Commissioner in 2024 and CEC in 2025, has repeatedly faced allegations from the Opposition that he has “favoured” the BJP.

Russell wary of Antonelli threat despite dominant Baku pole
BAKU, Sept 25 : George Russell refused to rule out Mercedes teammate Kimi Antonelli as a threat to his victory hopes in Saturday’s Azerbaijan Grand Prix, despite the Briton starting from pole and the championship leader 16th after a costly qualifying crash.
“Obviously, you can’t discount Kimi,” said Russell after eclipsing Ferrari’s Charles Leclerc, his closest challenger, by 0.837 seconds in Friday’s qualifying.
“You know, started 19th in Monza and now he’s in 16th, so, yeah, he should be leading by a few laps early this time,” joked Russell after Antonelli recovered to win his home Italian Grand Prix earlier this month.
Antonelli, who leads Russell by 81 points in the overall standings after 14 rounds, was sidelined in the opening phase of qualifying after he clobbered the barriers at the first corner and was forced to park up with a broken suspension.
The 20-year-old lost crucial track time after being hit by a hydraulics issue on the opening day of practice and has played catch up to Russell ever since.
The Briton in contrast has looked the more at ease and dialled-in of the Mercedes pair around the tricky Baku street circuit layout.
“I’ve been feeling in a great spot this whole weekend,” said Russell. “You know, as I’ve said recently, I’m just getting more and more on top of this car and what it requires, and it’s just all feeling more intuitive."
Antonelli’s mistake provides an opportunity for Russell to put a dent in his championship advantage.
The last time he had such a chance was at Monza, when he started on the front row with Antonelli at the back of the grid.
He finished second to the Italian then but is determined to convert this time out in Azerbaijan.
“I’m feeling good,” said Russell.
“I think we’re in a great place to go for the win but, of course, this is Baku and anything can happen ... but whatever happens, I feel confident that we can go for the win.”

- The claim that Danish officials played "Send in the Clowns" when U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio arrived at the signing of a U.S.-Denmark-Greenland agreement is unproven.
- The rumor stems from footage circulating online that social media users claimed showed Rubio entering the signing ceremony on Sept. 22, 2026, as Judy Collins' song "Send in the Clowns" played in the background.
- Two separate live streams of the event both showed that Collins' song did play while Rubio entered the signing ceremony with Greenland and Denmark's Ministers of Foreign Affairs. All three men were in frame while parts of the song that specifically mentioned clowns played.
- Therefore, the choice of "Send in the Clowns" was likely coincidental or accidental. If one delegation had chosen the song to mock another, it did not have the intended effect.
- A spokesperson for the Danish Ministry of Foreign Affairs said via email that "Denmark was not involved in selecting the music for the signing ceremony."
- Snopes will update this report if, or when, additional information surfaces. We asked the White House whether its officials chose the pre-ceremony music and await a reply. In the meantime, we leave this claim unrated.
A claim (archived) circulated online in September 2026 that Danish officials played the song "Send in the Clowns" when U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio arrived at the signing of a U.S.-Denmark-Greenland agreement.
The claim circulated after U.S. President Donald Trump, Danish Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen and Greenland's Prime Minister Jens-Frederik Nielsen signed the deal, which sought to end months of diplomatic squabble over Greenland, in New York City on Sept. 22, 2026.
For example, one Threads user wrote, "Listen, I'm not gonna say it's perfection, but the Danish delegation having 'Send in the Clowns' playing on the playlist as Marco Rubio entered to sign Denmark/Greenland stuff is very, very well played."
Other social media users shared the claim on Facebook (archived), Instagram (archived), X (archived), and Bluesky (archived). Some of those users posted a video that they claimed showed Rubio entering the room as "Send in the Clowns" played, suggesting Danish officials sought to embarrass or insult him. Snopes readers also contacted us about the claim.
Two separate live streams of the Sept. 22 signing event, which used two separate camera angles, showed that "Send in the Clowns" did play around the time Rubio and Greenland and Denmark's Ministers of Foreign Affairs Múte B. Egede and Lars Løkke Rasmussen entered the conference room where the ceremony was held.
A spokesperson for the Danish Ministry of Foreign Affairs said via email on Sept. 22, 2026, "Denmark was not involved in selecting the music for the signing ceremony." Snopes asked the White House whether its officials chose the pre-conference music and await a reply.
In the meantime, we leave this claim unrated.
What the streams showed
According to a livestream (archived) of the Sept. 22 signing event shared by MAGNO News, which said it provided "professionally licensed video content from accredited media providers," "Send in the Clowns" played as attendees at the signing ceremony were finding their seats.
The song started at time code 9:59 in the stream. Rubio, Egede and Rasmussen entered the room around time code 10:59 as Collins sang, "Isn't it bliss? Don't you approve? One who keeps tearing around, One who can't move. Where are the clowns? There ought to be clowns."
At time code 11:18, the camera panned to Rasmussen as Collins sang, "There ought to be clowns."
Later, at time code 12:22, Collins sang, "But where are the clowns? Send in the clowns. Don't bother, they're here," as the camera panned to Rubio and Rasmussen.
Finally, at time code 13:24, Collins sang, "But where are the clowns? There ought to be clowns. Well, maybe next year," as the camera focused on Rubio and Rasmussen.
Another livestream (archived) uploaded to YouTube by British newspaper The Guardian also included Collins' music.
"Send in the Clowns" started at time code 5:14 on the Guardian's stream. Egede and Rubio entered the frame at time code 6:24 as Collins sang "Where are the clowns? There ought to be clowns."
The song ended at time code 9:10, followed by the announcement and arrival of Trump, Frederiksen and Nielsen at time code 9:46.
Given the above, the choice of "Send in the Clowns" was likely coincidental or accidental. Officials for all three countries signing the deal were in frame while parts of the song that directly mentioned clowns played, meaning that if one delegation had chosen the song to mock another, it did not have the intended effect.
Additionally, Trump, Frederiksen and Nielsen entered the stage right after the song. Again, if one delegation had sought to call the head of another other a clown through Collins' song, that did not have the intended effect because the heads of all three delegations appeared together.
Greenland deal averts diplomatic crisis
Trump, Frederiksen and Nielsen's deal for Greenland followed months of threats by Trump to seize the Arctic island. Trump's wish to gain control of Greenland, which is an autonomous territory of Denmark, threatened the integrity of NATO in January 2026 when his administration refused to rule out using military force.
Both Denmark and the U.S. are NATO members. The alliance has an article that treats an attack on one member as an attack on all.
Negotiations for a new deal related to U.S. involvement in the island's affairs began in January and concluded with the signing in September.
According to the Associated Press, the deal allows the U.S. to expand its military presence on Greenland, but affirms the island's status as an autonomous territory of Denmark as well as Greenland's right to self-determination.
It also notes that non-NATO countries cannot open military installations on the island.
The Danish parliament will consider the deal, which can only come into force if that parliament approves it.

Union minister Nitin Gadkari on Friday pointed to India’s growing push to convert waste into fuel, saying Nagpur is producing 28 tonnes of compressed natural gas (CNG) every day from waste, and around 4,000 similar projects are being taken up across the country.
Speaking at a programme after launching Madhya Pradesh’s new public bus service with Chief Minister Mohan Yadav, Gadkari said such projects (converting waste into fuel) would help farmers earn additional income while reducing imports and pollution
Gadkari also cited ethanol as an example of how alternative fuels can help raise farmers' income and reduce India's dependence on petroleum imports. He said maize prices had risen from around ₹1,200 per quintal to ₹2,600 per quintal after ethanol production began.
“Today, the farmer is not only our ‘anna data’ (food provider) but also our ‘urja data’ (energy provider),” Gadkari said and added, "This is the meaning of swadeshi, self-reliance and independence"
India imports petroleum worth around ₹22 lakh crore, according to Gadkari, who called for greater use of domestic and cleaner fuel sources to reduce this dependence.
The minister said flex-fuel engines, capable of running on 100 per cent ethanol, were being developed, and vehicles using this technology would be introduced. The government was also promoting electric vehicles, while hydrogen-powered vehicles were under development.
"I travel in a hydrogen vehicle. Its name is Mirai, which means future," he said.
Noting that hydrogen buses would be introduced on 10 routes, the minister said the new bus service launched in Madhya Pradesh would provide safer, more affordable, and more accountable transport facilities, particularly to poorer sections of society.
"Poor people should get facilities. They should get better facilities in AC buses, and the ticket fare should be 30 per cent lower than that of diesel buses. This is our dream," he said.
Gadkari said the government wanted to make public transport more popular in India and pointed out that the transport sector accounted for a substantial share of pollution.
eth
He said the government was working on several measures to improve bus safety and quality, including stricter testing requirements before registration.
Gadkari said buses would also be made more accessible for persons with disabilities and senior citizens, with designs enabling easier boarding.
He said the government was promoting the scrapping of old vehicles and increasing the number of vehicle scrapping and testing centres.
Gadkari said 32 driving centres had been started in Madhya Pradesh to address the shortage of trained drivers.

The recent episode of Bigg Boss 20 witnessed a heated exchange between Qazi Touqeer and Isha Rikhi, with Isha breaking down in tears and claiming that Qazi had behaved aggressively towards her during the captaincy task. As the drama unfolded, Mahhi Vij suggested that Isha’s references to “trauma” could lead viewers to draw an automatic connection with her former husband, Badshah.
While discussing the situation with her fellow contestants, Mahhi questioned Isha’s reaction to the incident. She said, “Agar usne chillaya to tumhara kaun sa trauma hit ho gaya bhai.” Addressing Uditi Singh and Arishfa Khan, she added that everyone has experienced their own form of trauma, saying, “Everybody has gone through their own traumas.”
Mahhi then linked Isha’s emotional breakdown and her claims of experiencing “anxiety” over the incident with the possibility of viewers speculating about her past relationship. She said, “Aur phir aap yaha pe le ke aa rhe ho ki mera koi trauma hai. Kal to bahar log sochenge pata nahi Badshah ne iske sath kya kar diya.”
Calling out what she perceived as an indirect allegation, Mahhi added, “Aap to indirectly uske upar character accusation laga rahe ho yar.”
Mahhi further explained her point with an example, saying that if a woman says, “Mujhe thappad se trauma hai,” people could automatically associate it with her partner. She concluded, “This is not right.”
